claim: Issue #272 steps 1-3 are measured and recorded. Step 1: a bounded place-and-route sweep on a scratch copy of layout/pnr/slice.pnr.json (seed 2/3/4, utilization 35/45, core margin 0.95/1.05/1.10 each paired with the strap offsets that keep M5 edges on the 24 nm grid and M6 edges on the 32 nm grid, plus one margin-1.10 route with the committed M5 offset left in place), every point routed to scratch and measured at the pin against a byte-identical control, shows no in-flow setting clears a rule family: M5.W.3 stays at 14-57 per slice on every on-grid point, V4.M4.EN.1/V4.M5.EN.2 and M3.S.2 move only with the core size, and 3 of the 9 points (seed 2, seed 3, utilization 35) re-introduce the closed-#6596 off-grid router-M4 mode. The points that lower the total with no new rule family (utilization 45: 975 -> 924; margin 0.95: 975 -> 961; margin 1.10: 975 -> 969, where M1.S.3 is absent) clear no family and are recorded, not adopted (in-repo issue #290). Step 2: the M1.S.* pad-free split re-taken on the committed slice reproduces klayout-tools#6992's baseline (40 of 272 marker boxes pad-free by the box predicate), and attribution shows the whole family is the router's VIA_VIA12 M1 landing pad: deleting that one shape from a scratch copy removes all 272 markers, the 40 box-pad-free markers are a pad that merges into the cell's own pin metal and splits a long edge into tip-length edges, no isolated library master carries an M1.S.* marker, and the 0.9.2 request has no pin-access or detailed-route field that could move any of it. Step 3: M5.W.3 is attributed to the deck: every marker on the committed slice and on every sweep point that has one is a cross-polygon edge pair between a PDN strap edge and a separate minimum-width signal shape exactly 14, 16, 18 or 20 x 24 nm away, reproduced on a three-shape layout with the deck's own expression (filed as klayout-tools#7226); the one off-grid point reports 0 M5.W.3 with 32 M5.AUX.1, the r6 trade re-measured. The committed streams did not change; lane_column.r11.envelope.json (15,600 / 8) and slice_routed.r11.envelope.json (975 / 8, every marker serialized) re-take them at the pin with checkout-relative provenance that re-verifies klt drc --check on this host. Every remaining family is recorded by name and count with its open upstream disposition; nothing is waived, filtered or re-scoped. Layout results against a predictive PDK, not measurements. Not T1 item 3 evidence: the manifest still cites no DRC record and item 3 stays unmet.

m1_attribution.mechanism: every marker of the family is caused by the router's VIA_VIA12 M1 landing pad. In the 40 box-pad-free cases the pad overlaps the cell's own M1 pin shape 7-31 nm (edge to edge) away from the marker: the merged polygon's long edge (a 'side') is split into two tip-length edges, and one of them now pairs with a tip edge of the same cell under the tip-to-tip limit. In the isolated master that edge is long, the same pair is a 25 nm side-to-tip pair exactly at the M1.S.2 limit, and nothing fires. The marker box is the 1 nm projection overlap of the two edges and lands where neither edge belongs to the pad, so the box predicate calls it pad-free

masters.M1.S.3: a tie-high master, 33 boxes (18 on its variant copy)

m1_attribution.router_wire_involvement: none: the request routes signals on M2-M7 (set_routing_layers -signal M2-M7), the routed DEF carries no M1 signal segment, and the only top-level M1 is the followpin rail; r7's 'pad-free routed-wire tip pairs' wording was an inference from the box predicate, not a trace
m1_attribution.request_fields_at_the_pin: the 0.9.2 request has no pin-access or detailed-route field: its routing-adjacent keys are seed (also passed as detailed_route -or_seed), route_critical_nets_percentage, route_congestion_iterations, route_allow_congestion, max_antenna_repair_iterations, placement_density, io.layer_h/layer_v and library.route_layers; the generated route stage calls detailed_route with -output_drc/-output_maze/-or_seed only and never calls pin_access. Nothing in the request can move a marker that is intrinsic to a pad/cell-pin merge

m5w3_attribution.finding: every M5.W.3 marker is a cross-polygon edge pair: one vertical edge of a PDN strap and the facing edge of a separate 24 nm signal landing shape in the gap between two straps, exactly 336, 384 or 432 nm apart (strap 216 + router clearance 96/144/192 + signal 24), i.e. even multiples of 24 nm. No merged M5 polygon of that width exists and no marker box lies inside one polygon

synthetic_reproduction.layout: three boxes on one layer (um): (0,0; 0.216,1.0) wide shape, (0.312,0.4; 0.336,0.446) separate min-width shape, (0.6,0; 0.936,0.3) a real 336 nm-wide shape
synthetic_reproduction.deck_expression: vert(m).width((w + 0.25).nm, projection).with_distance(w.nm, (w + 0.25).nm) over w in 48..480 step 48
synthetic_reproduction.result: two edge pairs: the real 336 nm width and the cross-polygon pair (0.336,0.446;0.336,0.4)/(0,0.4;0,0.446); the polygon-aware m.width(...) on the same merged region reports the real width only

m5w3_attribution.consequence: the family is a deck-side cross-polygon pair, not a router landing-patch width; its count is route-dependent only through which on-track signal shapes land an even number of tracks from a strap edge, which is also why the off-grid strap offset of r6 drove it to zero without touching any signal geometry
